senses.definition: (Of food) intended to be eaten off the premises from which it was bought.
senses.example: I couldn't be bothered to cook, so I bought a takeaway curry.
senses.usage: Commonwealth, Hong-Kong, Ireland, Philippines, UK, not-comparable, sometimes
senses.register: Commonwealth, Hong-Kong, Ireland, Philippines, UK, not-comparable, sometimes

senses.definition: A restaurant that sells food to be eaten elsewhere.
senses.example: If you're hungry, there's a takeaway just around the corner.

senses.definition: A meal which has been purchased and has been carefully packaged as to be taken and consumed elsewhere.
senses.example: I fancy an Indian takeaway tonight.

senses.definition: The preliminary part of a golfer′s swing when the club is brought back away from the ball.
senses.example: One drill to help you work on the long, low takeaway is to place a tee, a coin, or even another ball just beyond your back foot (whatever you choose should be slightly inside your toe to promote a slightly inside swing path).

senses.definition: A concession made by a labor union in the course of negotiations.
An idea from a talk, presentation, etc., that the listener or reader should remember and consider.
senses.example: For example, one of the big takeaways for myself (even though I know better) is when I don′t review my goals daily I get sucked into what′s currently happening and easily get distracted from what′s most important.
